So the teal side needs no new blank, only art review + copy + creative. (c) Context: 0/11 rotation brands run any opener creative 33 days out (Drake is on 'Past Season Sale', Free Fly on 'End of Summer'). BOT RECOMMENDATION: if approved, approve TEAL-FIRST and drop or defer the dove half. 8 days to kill_date. + 31/07 TEAL HALF STRENGTHENS AGAIN, score held 3/5. (a) 'teal season' on Meta Ad Library (US, ACTIVE) returns ZERO hunting-apparel advertisers for the SECOND consecutive day, while the dove lane counted >=4 on 30/07. (b) First COMPLETE 90-SKU sweep of gritfell.com/collections/all confirms the asset position precisely: 'Early Teal' exists as a HAT ($34) but there is NO teal design on any shirt/polo/swim blank — so a teal-first approval can ship the hat immediately while apparel needs a design translation, not a new idea. Same sweep shows 0/90 SKUs carry sale pricing. (c) Radar context corrected: 0/11 rotation brands run opener-countdown creative, but Tom Beckbe now leads its homepage with 'Tom Beckbe x Ducks Unlimited' ($495 DU Fowler Vest, $375 DU Double Timber Bag) — the conservation-partnership language a species-art brand might otherwise reach for is being taken at the premium tier. (d) Howler and Tom Beckbe both discount ZERO, confirming the no-discount posture is normal above the mid tier. 7 days to kill_date. + 01/08 SCORE HELD 3/5, halves keep diverging. (a) DOVE HALF WEAKER AGAIN: the lane escalated OUT of the cheap POD tier — Ball and Buck, a heritage US hunting-apparel brand, created 'Dove Season Essentials from Ball and Bck' on 31/07, and Hunthide refreshed its whole creative set the same day. GritFell would now be entering behind both a POD wave and a heritage brand, still with no dove art. (b) TEAL HALF HOLDS: 'teal season' returns ZERO hunting-apparel advertisers for the THIRD straight day (30/07, 31/07, 01/08); one unresolved outdoors-named page with an untitled creative is counted on neither side. (c) NEW BLOCKER FOUND ON OUR SIDE: the /products/early-teal page opens, but its description says nothing whatsoever about the bird — it is pure blank spec ('Classic 5-panel baseball cap', 'Engineered for comfort. Built for the wild.'). So if teal-first is approved, the first task is NOT ads, it is rewriting the listing; and the standing question 'is the art a moment or a static portrait' still needs a human to open the image. (d) TIER CONTEXT WORSENED: DECOY came back online after a 7-day block and turns out to run 33 species-embroidery hats at $34.99 (no dove, no teal) — so the accessible species-art hat tier now holds FOUR brands at $34-36, two of which discount. (e) Coincidence worth using: 07/08 is both this item's kill_date and the USFWS Prairie Pothole comment deadline. 6 days to kill_date. + 02/08 TEAL HALF HOLDS, DOVE HALF UNCHANGED, score held 3/5. (a) 'teal season' (US, ACTIVE) returns ZERO hunting-apparel advertisers for the FOURTH consecutive day (30/07, 31/07, 01/08, 02/08). No NEW brand entered the dove lane today. (c) Teal remains unscoreable on arbitrage criterion C: a WebSearch for a 2026 teal season date returned only 2025 material, so there is still no primary date to anchor creative to - if teal-first is approved, the copy cannot state a date yet. (d) NEW SUPPORTING EVIDENCE from the CN gift sweep: the best-performing-looking hook in the entire dove lane is Hunthide's 'The gift he'll actually wear', which is a GIFT-BUYER hook, not a hunter hook - consistent with the Etsy finding that gift framing is where the money sits. This strengthens the case for framing any opener capsule at Megan rather than at Tom. 5 days to kill_date. + 03/08 SCORE DOWN 3/5 -> 2/5, KILL CRITERION (2) TRIGGERED ON THE TEAL HALF. Live verify of duckcamp.com/collections/game-series-hats today: the set is now 42 SKUs (recorded as 32 on 29/07) and it CONTAINS 'Blue Winged Teal Hat' in two colorways at $36, product page open and in stock. The 29/07 entry saying 'Duck Camp has NO dove/teal SKU' and therefore 'kill criterion (2) NOT triggered' is FALSIFIED. Whether the teal was added since 29/07 or missed in the earlier count cannot be determined and is not being guessed. This matters more than a routine re-score because since 30/07 this ledger has recommended TEAL-FIRST specifically on the premise that the teal lane was empty on BOTH product and paid. The paid half still holds: 'teal season' on Meta Ad Library returned ZERO hunting-apparel advertisers for the FIFTH straight day (30/07 through 03/08). The product half no longer holds. NOT dropped to 1/5 because three things survive: (a) the paid lane is still empty; (b) Duck Camp sells static species portraits named after the species, so the MOMENT (bird banking, flooded timber, pre-dawn) is still unclaimed; (c) Duck Camp is discounting 14 of 32 hats to $25 on its other collection while GritFell holds $34 with zero discount, which is exactly the S4 signal. GritFell is NOT behind on product - Early Teal $34 already exists and undercuts by $2 - but IS behind on story, because /products/early-teal copy still says nothing about the bird (verified 01/08). If approved, the first task is the listing rewrite, not ads. Kill criteria updated: (1) any PAID teal creative from Duck Camp or DECOY -> drop to 1/5 and close; (2) no primary 2026 teal date by 07/08 -> countdown framing unusable, switch to a product framing. 4 days to kill_date. pending.title: Numbered Species Drop — capsule species-art phat hanh danh so, so luong chot, zero discount (mechanics hoc tu Free Fly x Trout Unlimited)
pending.kill_criteria: (1) OPENER-CAPSULE-2026 bi reject -> mat vehicle gan nhat, xet lai; (2) xuat hien case limited-drop e/khong ban het o tier accessible (<$60) cho thay mechanics khong dich xuong duoi premium
pending.evidence: 27/07: FF x TU hoodie 'ONLY 500 AVAILABLE' featured homepage (species art + conservation + numbered scarcity, $98). 28/07: product page live = SOLD OUT ('Out of Stock $98', 'Only 0 left'); page states year-1 drop sold out in 24h; 2nd annual 2026 edition -> annual-franchise mechanics (restock-as-news + scarcity). Chua co case nao o tier <$60 — do la cau hoi mo. + 29/07: Duck Camp Game Series is an ALWAYS-ON program (not numbered, not capped) and 14/32 SKUs already discounted to $25 — so it is not a counter-example to limited/numbered mechanics at the sub-$60 tier. Score held 3/5. + 30/07: no new evidence for or against. Adjacent finding worth noting for whoever decides — GritFell already has 36 species-embroidery hats at one price with NO program name and NO season tag, while Duck Camp bundles 32 into 'Game Series / New for Fall 26'. A named program is the cheapest version of this mechanic and needs no price or scarcity change. Score held 3/5, 22 days to kill_date. + 31/07: mild support, score held 3/5. Complete 90-SKU sweep shows 0/90 GritFell SKUs have ever carried sale pricing — the no-discount discipline a numbered/limited drop depends on is already the brand's actual operating posture, so the mechanic would not require a behaviour change. Independently, both T6 rotation brands (Howler $75-145, Tom Beckbe $195-495) also run zero discounts, i.e. no-discount is the norm above the mid tier rather than an eccentric stance. Still NO observed case of numbered/limited mechanics at the sub-$60 tier — that remains the open question. 21 days to kill_date. + 01/08: the open question finally has a data point, and it cuts against the premise. DECOY (unblocked today after 7 days) discounts a $34.99 Corduroy Rope Hat to $17.49 — a ~50% cut inside GritFell's own hat tier. Together with Duck Camp (14 of 32 Game Series hats at $25), there are now TWO independent precedents for deep discounting at the sub-$60 accessible tier. Reading: numbered/limited scarcity mechanics have still never been OBSERVED at this tier, and the tier's actual norm is discounting, not scarcity. That does not kill the idea — it reframes it: GritFell's 0/90-never-discounted posture is a deliberate difference rather than the tier standard, so a numbered drop would be a way of SAYING that difference out loud. Caveat found the same day: the brand's no-discount posture is real on unit price but NOT on offer, since the site runs 'BUY 2 GET 1 FREE' in the banner and a conflicting 'BUY 2, SAVE 15%' on product pages. Score held 3/5, 20 days to kill_date. + 02/08 A CHEAPER RIVAL MECHANIC APPEARED, score held 3/5. Atwoods Ranch & Home Goods is running 'Shop This Week's Hunt Drop' alongside 'New gear. New savings. Every Friday.' (both created 31/07) - a fixed-weekday cadence that produces the same 'come back, it is new' effect with NO quantity commitment, NO numbering and NO tooling. That does not kill the numbered drop, but it does supply a reversible, near-zero-cost alternative that should be tested first, since the numbered version commits inventory while the cadence version commits only a calendar slot. Recommendation if the human wants the scarcity effect without the risk: trial a fixed weekday first, and reserve numbering for a capsule that genuinely has a fixed quantity. 19 days to kill_date.

pending.evidence: 02/08 (proposed): Gulf Coast Fishing Report dated 01-02/08 came back live after 6 stale days and lists the surf/beach bite as whiting, pompano, bluefish. Verified live the same day on gritfell.com/collections/hat, species by species: pompano NO, flounder NO, amberjack NO, Spanish mackerel NO, snapper NO, whiting NO, bluefish NO - 7 of the 9 species currently biting have zero SKU. Structural point: the catalog covers BOTH ENDS of the distance-from-shore axis (offshore: Offshore Marlin, King Mackerel Strike, Tarpon Season; inshore/freshwater: Bass Strike, Topwater Strike, Brown Trout, Brookie King, Copper Tail Redfish) and leaves the middle empty. Why this middle is worth more than its size: surf is the only fishing scene in which the gift buyer is physically present - offshore is the trip she is left home from - which lines up with the same day's Etsy finding that gift framing carries the $25-79 band. Arbitrage gate: S PASS, E PASS (K2 cross-hatch naturalist, 3 threads Bone White #F4F1EA / Iron Charcoal #2A2A28 / Aged Tan #C9A87A, 7x13cm front tonal, ~3-4K stitches), A PASS (hat -> tier social), C PASS, T4 (fishing report tier has spoken, editorial silent, 0/90 SKUs; deliberately not T5 because the CN rotation cannot verify 0/11 brands). Video angle: macro of water pulling off sand to reveal the trough -> hat rotating in raking light with the Aged Tan fin thread catching -> pull back to a planted rod and an adult-plus-child shadow; hook 'The first trough, before anyone else is up.' HONEST CAVEAT: pompano/whiting/bluefish are not on the 01 core-niche list, but neither are tarpon, marlin, sailfish, king mackerel or snook, all of which the brand already sells - so this is a documentation gap needing human confirmation, not a doctrine rejection. Human approval required before any art brief.

pending.evidence: 03/08 arbitrage gate PASS at T4. Source: Gulf Coast Fishing Report opened live 03/08 (tier 3, earliest species source) lists speckled trout FIRST under inshore AND again under surf/beach ('worked before sunrise') - the only species named twice in the edition. Both sides verified live today: gritfell.com/search?q=trout returns 5 SKUs, ALL freshwater (Brown Trout $34, Rainbow Trout $34, Hooked on Trout swim short $39 / polo $50 / button shirt $55) - no speckled or spotted seatrout in any format. Duck Camp's 42-SKU Game Series carries brown, rainbow and brook trout, also all freshwater. So the number-one inshore species of the Gulf coast, biting right now, is missing from BOTH GritFell and the strongest species-art competitor - while both already sell 2-3 freshwater trout designs, making this a gap directly adjacent to something already selling rather than a new lane. Doctrine: 'seatrout' IS on the brand's own target-species list in 01, so unlike the 02/08 pompano/whiting idea this needs no doctrine waiver - materially lower risk. Gate detail: S pass (specific subject and moment, not 'inshore fishing'); E pass (elongated body, black spots on silver-green translate directly into stitch dots, no gradient; 7x13cm, ~3-4K stitches, K2 cross-hatch, 3 threads Bone White / Iron Charcoal / Aged Tan from 01 section 5); A pass (works on hat -> tier social, and extends onto the existing 'Hooked on' shirt family without a new blank); C pass (no licensed camo, no IP, season matches the live report). T scored 4 not 5 because today's Monday sweep opened homepages and main collections of all 11 brands but not every full catalog, so '0/11 at SKU level' cannot be claimed. Output logged in B7: hat concept FIRST LIGHT SPECK ($34, 5-panel) plus a 5-15s texture-in-motion video angle, hook 'Before the sun. Before anyone.'
